context: The overall root, 1, has left child 0 and right child 4. Node 4 has only right child 5, and 5 has only right child 6. The figure labels unbalanced node 4 as node and its right child 5 as child.

The balance factor is the height of the left subtree minus the height of the right. A leaf has height 0 and an empty subtree has height −1. A tree is balanced only if the absolute value of every node's balance factor is at most 1. The factors below follow from the connections in the figure.
description: The three panels show the tree before rotation, after the local rotation, and after reconnection to the parent. Each depicts a stage rather than an individual assignment in code. Initially, node 4 has left and right subtree heights −1 and 1, giving it a balance factor of −2. The overall root 1 also has balance factor −2.
The left rotation promotes 5 to local root. Node 4 becomes its left child and 6 remains its right child. Since 5 originally had no left child, 4 has no right child after the rotation.

The middle panel shows only three solid edges: 1→0, 5→4, and 5→6. No solid edge yet connects parent 1 to the new root 5. A dashed circle at the old position of 4 and a dashed edge from there to 5 show the arrangement before rotation. They do not represent an extra node or a current connection. The final panel adds 1→5 and removes the dashed marks.

Node 5 has left child 4 and right child 6. Nodes 0, 4, and 6 are leaves. The right subtree of 1 drops to height 1, the entire tree regains balance, and the inorder sequence remains [0, 1, 4, 5, 6].
steps.key_state: After reconnection, root 1 has left child 0 and right child 5. Node 5 has left child 4 and right child 6. The whole tree is balanced.
